body:
Coordinator continuation-wake and hold-ownership lessons, from Fable2's Oct9–18 missed-wake incidents (full chronology remains in revisions1–10). When a worker ends a turn waiting for the coordinator, its final answer may exist only in its transcript. For a multi-turn instruction, name the actual next event and who supplies its continuation; require the worker's one-line report when it ends waiting. A promise to act 'next turn' alone does not create that turn. Process completion notifications and settled task evidence promptly; where the current host already supplies a continuation, account for that before adding another wake. Use supported session/task/mail reads to resolve an overdue report, within current authority, rather than assuming work continued or reading another owner's worktree.

A durableButNotWoken send receipt does not establish a missed wake, a dead worker or failed execution. Read the original exact message's current status and relevant reply before reassigning or duplicating work; preserve original message/key/route for unresolved retries. Do not treat historical five-minute watchdog examples as a new timer or automatic launch/resume rule.

Hold-ownership lesson preserved from termal-window16 r12 (Oct18 03:06Z; Advisor #1120/#1121): every coordinator hold names its blocker and explicit release condition on the owning work item, and names who supplies the continuation. State a self-release condition only when it is already explicitly authorized; otherwise retain coordinator ownership. Never leave a worker waiting on an unnamed release event. Current host/backend completion-wake, receipt-ACK and task authority govern. This keeper grants no new dispatch, session resume/cancel, process control, peer-root access or resource window.
